Although external claims that the starting price of iPhone 18 Pro is US$1,399 are likely exaggerated, there is no doubt that the price of this year's entire iPhone lineup will see a substantial hike.

Apple has laid the groundwork for the impending 'price shock' through its all-new Apple Upgrade installment plan, and T-Mobile has promptly responded by launching a brand-new 3-year installment payment plan...

In June this year, Apple implemented significant price increases on most of its products in response to the sharp rise in memory costs. Existing iPhone models were not included in the price hikes, but it is almost certain that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be priced higher than last year's equivalent models.

The Apple Upgrade rental plan allows users to get their hands on all kinds of products at a lower monthly fee, and the iPhone is certainly included. However, the biggest 'catch' is that: once the payment period ends, you do not actually own the product. Many customers may ultimately find themselves trapped in an endless cycle of Apple Upgrade renewals.

T-Mobile will launch a brand-new installment payment plan tomorrow, allowing customers to spread the cost of their iPhone and all related fees over 3 years rather than 2. Dubbed EIP Flex 36, the plan is marketed with zero interest and zero down payment.

It is worth noting that there are two附加 conditions: the zero down payment and zero interest apply only to customers with good credit ratings. The fine print also states that some customers may face an effective annual percentage rate as high as 24%. However, if you qualify and plan to keep using a new iPhone for the next three years or more, this may still be a rather attractive option.
